items.title: The Five Fields of Knowledge, and Why Inner Teaching Reveals an Enduring Yet Changeable Karma

items.zh: 如是一切明處所攝有五明處。一、內明處，二、因明處，三、聲明處，四、醫方明處，五、工業明處。菩薩於此五種明處若正勤求，則名勤求一切明處。
items.en: Everything comprised within these fields of knowledge falls into five: first, inner teaching; second, logic; third, linguistics; fourth, medicine; and fifth, practical crafts. When bodhisattvas correctly and diligently seek out these five fields, this is called diligently seeking every field of knowledge.

items.zh: 諸佛語言，名內明論，此幾相轉？如是乃至一切世間工巧業處，名工業明論，此幾相轉？
謂內明論略二相轉。一者、顯示正因果相，二者、顯示已作不失、未作不得相。
items.en: Inner teaching, in brief, operates through two aspects: first, revealing the genuine workings of cause and effect; and second, revealing that what has genuinely been done is never lost, while what has never been done is never attained.

items.title: The Origins of Buddhist Logic, and Its Two Practical Functions

items.zh: 因明論亦二相轉。一者、顯示摧伏他論勝利相，二者、顯示免脫他論勝利相。
items.en: Logic likewise operates through two aspects: first, revealing the mark of victoriously defeating a rival's argument; and second, revealing the mark of successfully escaping a rival's own attack.

items.title: Linguistics' Two Aspects, and How One Million Verses Became Three Hundred

items.zh: 聲明論亦二相轉。一者、顯示安立界相、能成立相；二者、顯示語工勝利相。
items.en: Linguistics likewise operates through two aspects: first, revealing the establishment of the basic elements of sound and what makes them combinable into meaning; and second, revealing the mark of skilful excellence in speech itself.

items.title: Section: Medicine's Four Aspects Mirror the Four Noble Truths

items.zh: 醫方明論四種相轉。一者、顯示病體善巧相，二者、顯示病因善巧相，三者、顯示斷已生病善巧相，四者、顯示已斷之病當不更生善巧相。
items.en: Medicine operates through four aspects: first, revealing skill regarding the nature of illness itself; second, revealing skill regarding the cause of illness; third, revealing skill in curing an illness once it has arisen; and fourth, revealing skill in ensuring a cured illness never arises again.

items.title: Practical Crafts' Single Aspect, Closing the Account of All Five Fields

items.zh: 一切世間工業明論，顯示各別工巧業處所作成辦種種異相。
items.en: Every worldly practical craft reveals the various distinct outcomes accomplished by each specific trade and skill.

items.title: Section: The Ten Causes Open — A Complete Account of Causality Itself

items.zh: 云何內明論顯示正因果相？謂有十種因，當知建立無顛倒因，攝一切因。或為雜染、或為清淨、或為世間彼彼稼穡等無記法轉。
items.en: How does inner teaching reveal the genuine workings of cause and effect? It should be understood that there are ten kinds of cause, establishing a complete and undistorted account of cause that comprises every cause whatsoever — whether operating to produce defilement, purity, or neutral phenomena such as this or that worldly crop.

items.zh: 云何十因？一隨說因，二、觀待因，三、牽引因，四、攝受因，五、生起因，六、引發因，七、定別因，八、同事因，九、相違因，十、不相違因。
items.en: What are the ten causes? First, the cause of expression; second, the cause of dependence; third, the cause of distant attraction; fourth, the cause of supportive embrace; fifth, the cause of immediate arising; sixth, the cause of induced extension; seventh, the cause of determinate distinction; eighth, the cause of shared activity; ninth, the cause of opposition; and tenth, the cause of non-opposition.

items.title: The First Four Causes: Language, Dependence, Distant Attraction, and Supportive Conditions

items.zh: 謂一切法，名為先故想，想為先故說。是名彼諸法隨說因。
items.en: Regarding all phenomena: name comes first, enabling thought; thought comes first, enabling speech. This is called the cause of expression for those phenomena.

items.zh: 觀待此故，此為因故，於彼彼事若求、若取，此名彼觀待因。如觀待手故，手為因故，有執持業。觀待足故，足為因故，有往來業。觀待節故，節為因故，有屈申業。觀待飢渴故，飢渴為因故，於諸飲食若求、若取。
items.en: Depending on this, this becomes the cause by which this or that thing is sought or obtained — this is called the cause of dependence. Depending on the hand, the hand becomes the cause of the activity of grasping. Depending on the foot, the foot becomes the cause of the activity of walking. ... Depending on hunger and thirst, hunger and thirst become the cause for seeking and obtaining food and drink.

items.zh: 隨如是等無量道理，應當了知觀待因相。
一切種子，望後自果，名牽引因。除種子外，所餘諸緣，名攝受因。
items.en: Every seed, with respect to its own fruit still to come, is called the cause of distant attraction. ... Everything other than the seed itself is called the cause of supportive embrace.

items.title: Section: Causes Five Through Seven — Immediate Arising, the Domino Effect, and Why Melon Seeds Never Yield Beans

items.zh: 即諸種子，望初自果，名生起因。即初種子所生起果，望後種子所牽引果，名引發因。
items.en: These very seeds, with respect to their most immediate fruit, are called the cause of immediate arising. ... The fruit first arisen from that seed, with respect to the further fruit later drawn out by a subsequent seed, is called the cause of induced extension.

items.zh: 種種異類，各別因緣，名定別因。
items.en: Each distinct kind of phenomenon has its own distinct, separate cause and condition — this is called the cause of determinate distinction.

items.title: Causes Eight Through Ten Complete the Ten-Fold Framework

items.zh: 若觀待因、若牽引因、若攝受因、若生起因、若引發因、若定別因，如是諸因總攝為一，名同事因。
items.en: The cause of dependence, the cause of distant attraction, the cause of supportive embrace, the cause of immediate arising, the cause of induced extension, and the cause of determinate distinction — all these causes gathered together as one are called the cause of shared activity.

items.zh: 於所生法能障礙因，名相違因。此障礙因若闕、若離，名不相違因。
items.en: Whatever is capable of obstructing a phenomenon about to arise is called the cause of opposition. When this obstructing cause is lacking or absent, this is called the cause of non-opposition.

items.title: Section: Six Everyday Meanings of "Opposition" — and Which One Actually Defines the Ninth Cause

items.zh: 當知相違略有六種。一、語言相違。謂有一類，或諸沙門、或婆羅門，所造諸論前後相違。二、道理相違。謂為成立諸所成立諸所知義，建立比量，不與證成道理相應。三、生起相違。謂所生法，能生緣闕，障生緣會。四、同處相違。謂明、闇、貪、瞋、苦、樂等法。五、怨敵相違。謂毒蛇、鼠狼、猫狸、鼷鼠，互為怨敵、惡知識等。六、障治相違。謂修不淨與諸貪欲，修慈與瞋，
items.en: It should be understood that opposition has, in brief, six kinds. First, verbal opposition ... second, logical opposition ... third, opposition of arising, where a phenomenon about to arise lacks the conditions able to produce it, or meets conditions that obstruct its arising. Fourth, opposition of shared location, as with light and darkness, craving and hatred, pain and pleasure. Fifth, opposition of natural enemies ... sixth, opposition of remedy and obstruction, as when cultivating contemplation on impurity opposes craving, or cultivating loving-kindness opposes hatred ...

items.zh: 修悲與害，修七覺支、八聖道支與三界繫一切煩惱。
於此義中，正意唯取生起相違。
items.en: Within this discussion, the precise intended meaning refers only to opposition of arising.

items.title: Reducing Ten Causes to Two, and Mapping Them Onto the Four Classical Conditions

items.zh: 此一切因二因所攝。一、能生因，二、方便因。當知此中，牽引種子、生起種子名能生因；所餘諸因名方便因。
items.en: All these causes are comprised within two: first, generative cause; second, facilitating cause. It should be understood that the seed of distant attraction and the seed of immediate arising are called generative cause, while every remaining cause is called facilitating cause.

items.zh: 復有四緣。一、因緣，二、等無間緣，三、所緣緣，四、增上緣。當知此中，若能生因，是名因緣；若方便因，是增上緣。
items.en: There are, moreover, four conditions: first, causal condition; second, immediately-preceding condition; third, object condition; and fourth, dominant condition. ... It should be understood that generative cause here corresponds to causal condition, while facilitating cause corresponds to dominant condition.

items.zh: 等無間緣及所緣緣，唯望一切心心法說。由彼一切心及心法前生開導所攝受故，所緣境界所攝受故，方生方轉。是故當知等無間緣及所緣緣，攝受因攝。如是十因，云何能令一切世間種種事轉？云何能令雜染事轉？云何能令清淨事轉？

blocks.text: The five sciences a bodhisattva studies (Days 103–124 treated them at length), then the ten causes, a summary of the treatise's theory of causation (compare Day 34).

Inner (Buddhist) knowledge; logic; linguistics; medicine; crafts. **Inner knowledge** reveals "the genuine workings of cause and effect", and "that what has been done is never lost, and what has not been done is never attained". **Logic**: "defeating a rival's argument, and escaping a rival's attack". **Linguistics**: the elements of sound and their combination, and skill in expression. Venerable Miào Jìng: by tradition Brahmā composed a million verses of grammar, later reduced to eight hundred, then to three hundred. **Medicine** mirrors the four truths: "the nature of illness, its cause, its cure, and ensuring it does not return". **Crafts**: the outcomes of each trade.

The cause of **expression** ("name comes first, enabling thought; thought comes first, enabling speech"); of **dependence** ("depending on the hand, grasping"); of **distant attraction** (a seed towards its future fruit); of **supportive embrace** (all conditions other than the seed); of **immediate arising** (a seed towards its immediate fruit); of **induced extension** (fruit leading to further fruit); of **determinate distinction** ("each kind has its own distinct cause"; melon seeds never yield beans); of **cooperation** (all these together); of **opposition** (what obstructs arising); of **non-opposition** (its absence).
Verbal, logical, of arising, of shared location ("light and darkness, craving and hatred"), and others; here, opposition of arising is meant.
The ten reduce to **generative** and **facilitating** causes, and map onto the four conditions: causal, immediately preceding, object, dominant.

quiz.q: Inner teaching shows "done is never lost, undone never attained." Does "never lost" mean permanent, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: not lost doesn't mean unchanging — it still grows or wanes; without the bodhisattva path, no buddhahood
quiz.why: "Second, revealing that what has genuinely been done is never lost, while what has never been done is never attained." Master Cháng Bǎi: not being lost doesn't mean permanent and unchanging — it still increases and decreases. What isn't done certainly isn't there — e.g., without practising the bodhisattva path, one certainly can't become a buddha.

quiz.q: Linguistics: Brahmā first composed a million verses. How far was it reduced, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
quiz.why: "Linguistics likewise operates through two aspects." Venerable Miào Jìng: later a sage reduced it to 800 verses; later another reduced it to 300. (Brahmā first composed a million.)

quiz.q: Medicine "operates through four aspects." How does the Ground of Learning explain it, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: usually medicine; the Ground of Learning says it's the four noble truths
quiz.why: "Medicine operates through four aspects: skill regarding the nature of illness, its cause, curing it, and ensuring it never recurs." Master Cháng Bǎi: medicine is usually explained as medical science; the Ground of Learning says it's suffering, origin, cessation, and path.

quiz.q: The ten causes operate "for defilement, purity, or neutral phenomena." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain defilement and purity?
options: defilement is worldly cause and effect; purity supramundane
quiz.why: "Ten kinds of cause … whether operating to produce defilement, purity, or neutral phenomena such as this or that worldly crop." Venerable Miào Jìng: "defilement" is worldly cause and effect; "purity" is supramundane cause and effect.

quiz.q: "Name first enables thought, thought enables speech — the cause of expression." What example does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: someone says "I'm taking today off," and doesn't come
quiz.why: "Regarding all phenomena: name comes first, enabling thought; thought comes first, enabling speech. This is called the cause of expression." Master Cháng Bǎi: say someone says, "I'm taking leave today" — having said it, he doesn't come today.

quiz.q: "Each distinct kind has its own cause — the cause of determinate distinction." The note reads it as the ten causes not mixing. What do the lectures say?
options: Cháng Bǎi: melons from melons, barley from barley; Miào Jìng: compassion brings long life, not wisdom — each has its own cause
quiz.why: "Each distinct kind of phenomenon has its own distinct, separate cause and condition — this is called the cause of determinate distinction." Master Cháng Bǎi: plant melons, get melons; plant beans, get beans; a barley seed yields barley sprouts — never rice. Venerable Miào Jìng: compassion protecting beings brings long life, not wisdom — each has its own causes. The note's "the ten causes don't mix" is wrong.

quiz.q: "All these causes are comprised in two: generative and facilitating." How does Master Cháng Bǎi divide them?
options: the seeds of distant attraction and immediate arising are generative; the other eight facilitating
quiz.why: "All these causes are comprised within two: first, generative cause; second, facilitating cause … the seed of distant attraction and the seed of immediate arising are called generative cause." Master Cháng Bǎi: the seed of distant attraction is that cause, the seed of immediate arising is that cause — together the generative cause; the other eight are facilitating causes.
